summary: New Azure customers can create a free account with a $200 credit to use on Azure services within 30 days, plus monthly free amounts of popular services for 12 months and always-free services. Microsoft states the credit card is used for verification and will not be charged for the trial (a temporary authorization may apply). After 30 days or when the credit is exhausted, you must move to pay-as-you-go to keep using services. Distinct from Azure for Students. Limit: one free account with $200 credit per new customer. Trial credit cannot be spent on Azure Marketplace offers or Spot Virtual Machines and cannot be combined with Azure Hybrid Benefit; sovereign-cloud products are excluded.
claim_steps: Sign up at azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/ as a new Azure customer.
Complete identity verification (phone and typically a credit/debit card; Microsoft says the card is not charged for the trial aside from a possible temporary authorization).

Use the $200 credit within 30 days on eligible services, plus listed free-service amounts. Marketplace offers and Spot Virtual Machines are not covered; Azure Hybrid Benefit cannot be combined with the trial credit.
Upgrade to pay-as-you-go before the credit or 30-day window ends if you need to keep running workloads.

social_proof.title: Azure free-account Marketplace exclusion
social_proof.text: No, your Azure free account credit can’t be applied to Azure Marketplace offers and you can only purchase products on Azure Marketplace once you’ve moved to pay-as-you-go pricing.
